outcome: Composite adverse perinatal outcome (perinatal mortality or serious neonatal morbidity; five minute APGAR score ≤4, neurological abnormality and need for intubation)
Composite maternal adverse outcome (major haemorrhage, trauma or infection)
cohort: 534 sets of twins ≥32 + 0 weeks of gestation from a single tertiary centre over nine years
finding: There were no significant differences in composite adverse perinatal or maternal outcomes between women with twin pregnancies ≥32 weeks gestation who had a planned vaginal birth compared to those who had a planned cesarean section.
mod_finding: This study compared outcomes in twin pregnancies with planned vaginal birth or planned cesarean section, finding no significant differences in adverse outcomes.
